humanities_role_explanation: Items are drawn from 2024 Irish Leaving Certificate exams across 12 subjects (mostly STEM and business, with History, Politics & Society, Art as a minority). The competence tested is general academic reasoning and multilingual transfer in Irish vs English, not humanities disciplinary competence.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text questions in parallel Irish and English; 18.11% of samples include graphical illustrations (figures, tables, diagrams) that models must interpret alongside text.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Long-form open-ended generation answering exam questions, graded against official marking schemes ('factual correctness, domain-specific academic knowledge, linguistic fidelity, and depth of reasoning'). Includes math/physics/chemistry reasoning, multimodal diagram questions, parallel Irish-English comparison for multilingual transfer (language fidelity via FastText), and self-reported confidence calibration analysis.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Broad multi-subject benchmark of 12 subjects in four groups, evaluating open-ended academic reasoning across languages.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: o4-mini, gpt-4.1, gemini-2.0-flash, Llama-4-Scout-Instruct, aya-vision-32b, aya-vision-8b.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy via binary LLM-as-judge (gemini-2.5-flash) against marking schemes; language fidelity percentage; confidence vs accuracy.

summary: IRLBench is a parallel Irish-English multimodal benchmark of 1700 question-marking-scheme samples from the 2024 Irish Leaving Certificate, framed as open-ended generation and judged by an LLM against official marking schemes. Evaluations of six LLMs/VLMs show a persistent English-Irish gap and weak Irish language fidelity.
key_findings: Best English accuracy 76.2% (o4-mini); best Irish accuracy 58.43% (gpt-4.1), o4-mini 55.82% in Irish. Gap exceeds 10% for all models (o4-mini 20.4%, gemini-2.0-flash 17.9%, gpt-4.1 12.9%). aya-vision models nearly fail in Irish. Most models produce valid Irish under 80% of the time (except gpt-4.1). Models are overconfident (>80% confidence vs <60% accuracy).
facets_explanation: Reference answers are the official Leaving Certificate marking schemes, extracted by gemini-2.0-flash and verified by human annotators for duplication, typos and missing pairs. The judge assigns a binary correct/incorrect label against the scheme. The same content is given in both languages with one key; answering requires external academic knowledge.
results_explanation: The paper states 'the top-performing model, o4-mini, achieves a strong average accuracy of 76.2%' in English and Table 3 gives 76.17. English vs Irish on the same questions: o4-mini has a gap of '20.4%' (reported as 20, upper figure). No human baseline is reported. Evaluation set is all 1700 samples (850 per language is derived from 'equally distributed'). The Irish-language performance deficit is stated as a finding.
